(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] | highlights = *[[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish League]] MVP ([[2020–21 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2021]]) *Turkish Junior League champion (2019) | bbr = | nba_profile = | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|TUR}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|FIBA Europe U-16 Championship]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2018 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|2018 Serbia]]|[[Turkish men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Under-16]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|FIBA Europe U-18 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2019 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|2019 Greece]]|[[Turkish men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Under-18]]}} }} '''Alperen Şengün''' (born 25 July 2002) is a [[Turkey|Turkish]] professional [[basketball]] player for [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]]. He also represents the senior [[Turkish national basketball team|Turkish national team]]. ==Early life and youth career== Alperen Şengün was born in [[Giresun]], northeastern Turkey, on 25 July 2002. His parents wanted him to begin working in the [[Swimming (sport)|sport of swimming]]. However, Şengün preferred the sport of basketball, as he had watched his older brother play the sport. So, at the age of eight, he started playing basketball. Early on, he actually competed in both sports at the same time. However, due to practical issues, like a lack of necessary time that was needed to properly train for both sports, he had to choose one of them. He decided to continue with basketball. ===Giresun University (2012–2014)=== In 2012, Şengün began playing [[youth system]] basketball with the youth teams of the sports club of [[Giresun University]], where he played until 2014. ===Banvit (2014–2019)=== After his discovery by head coach Ahmet Gürgen, during a youth sports festival, Şengün moved from [[Giresun]] to [[Bandırma]], to join the youth teams of the Turkish club [[Bandırma B.İ.K.|Bandırma]], which was then known as Banvit. By August 2014, he had signed a youth contract with Banvit. In the 2018–19 season, while competing with Banvit's juniors, Şengün eventually won the Turkish Basketball Junior League championship (which was established in 2017). Şengün was also named the Turkish Junior League's [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]]. ==Professional career== ===Bandırma Kırmızı (2018–2019)=== Şengün began his professional [[sports club|club]] career in the 2018–19 TBL season with [[Bandırma Kırmızı BK|Bandırma Kırmızı]], of the second division [[Turkish Basketball First League|Turkish First League (TBL)]]. In 29 games played in Turkey's 2nd division, he averaged 10.8 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 0.8 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game, in 21.9 minutes per game. He shot 47.6 percent from the field overall, 53.6 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 25.9 percent on 3-point field goal attempts, and 60.0 percent from the free-throw line.[https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/175107/alperen-sengun ALPEREN SENGUN Basketball Career Averages 18-19.] ===Teksüt Bandırma (2019–2020)=== Şengün joined the first division [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League (BSL)]] club [[Bandırma B.İ.K.|Teksüt Bandırma]], for the [[2019–20 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2019–20 BSL season]]. In 22 games played in Turkey's 1st division, he averaged 5.0 points, 3.9 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.4 blocks per game, in 13.5 minutes per game. He shot 51.1 percent from the field overall, 57.5 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 0–10 (0.00 percent) on 3-point field goal attempts, and 58.6 percent from the free-throw line.[https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/175107/alperen-sengun ALPEREN SENGUN Basketball Career Averages 19-20.][http://www.tblstat.net/pd.asp?p=3076&s=1920 Sengun, Alperen 2019-2020 Season.] He also played in one of Europe's two secondary level competitions, the [[FIBA Champions League]]. During the [[2019–20 FIBA Champions League|2019–20 BCL season]], he averaged 6.6 points, 3.3 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.3 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game, in 14.9 minutes per game, in 15 games played. He shot 48.0 percent from the field overall, 53.6 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 31.6 percent 3-point field goal attempts, and 63.6 percent from the free-throw line.[https://www.championsleague.basketball/19-20/player/Alperen-Sengun Alperen SENGUN STATISTICS.] ===Beşiktaş (2020–present)=== In August 2020, Şengün signed a three-year contract with the Turkish club [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]].{{cite web|title=Alperen Şengün Beşiktaş'ta|url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/79270/alperen-sengun-besiktasta.html|work=bjk.com.tr|language=Turkish|date=7 August 2020|accessdate=8 August 2020}} He had an excellent regular season with Beşiktaş, as he averaged 19.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.7 blocks, in 28.3 minutes per game, in 29 games played in the [[Basketball Super League]].[http://www.tblstat.net/pd.asp?p=3076&s=2021 Sengun, Alperen 2020-2021 Season Regular Season Statistics.] On May 12, 2021, he was named the MVP of the BSL's regular season.{{cite web |title= Alperen Sengun named Turkish BSL 2020-21 season MVP |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/tbl/1205414/alperen-sengun-named-turkish-bsl-2020-21-season-mvp/ |website=Eurohoops.net |date=12 May 2021|accessdate=13 May 2021}} On the same day, he announced his decision to enter [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Alperen Sengun, No. 14 basketball prospect in ESPN Top 100, to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31432025/alperen-sengun-no-14-prospect-espn-top-100-enter-nba-draft |website=ESPN.com |date=12 May 2021|accessdate=13 May 2021}} Overall, in Turkey's [[2020–21 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2020–21 BSL season]] (regular season and playoffs), in 28.1 minutes per game, he averaged 18.6 points, 8.9 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.5 blocks, in 34 games played. He shot 62.6 percent from the field overall, 66.7 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 21.2 percent on 3-point field goal attempts, and 81.2 percent from the free-throw line.[https://www.tbf.org.tr/ligler/bsl-2020-2021/basketbolcu-detay/260291 ALPEREN ŞENGÜN 25.07.2002 TÜRKİYE İSTATİSTİK ÖZETİ {{in lang|tr}}.] He also played with Beşiktaş in the fourth-level European-wide competition, the [[FIBA Europe Cup]]. In the Europe Cup's [[2020–21 FIBA Europe Cup|2020–21 season]], in 29.7 minutes per game, he averaged 23.0 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.7 steals and 2.0 blocks, in 3 games played. He shot 71.0 percent from the field overall, 75.9 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 0–2 (0.00 percent) on 3-point field goal attempts, and 69.4 percent from the free-throw line.[http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/20-21/player/Alperen-Sengun Alperen SENGUN Besiktas ICRYPEX (TUR).] ==National team career== ===Turkish junior team=== Şengün competed with the [[Turkey men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Turkish junior under-16 national team]] at the [[2018 FIBA Under-16 European Championship]], which was held in [[Novi Sad, Serbia]], where he finished the competition by winning the bronze medal. Şengün was also selected to the competition's [[2018 FIBA Under-16 European Championship#Awards|All-Tournament Team]]. In seven games played during the tournament, he averaged 14.4 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.6 steals, and 1.4 blocks per game, in 24.9 minutes per game. He shot 56.9 percent from the field overall, 61.9 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 22.2 percent on 3-point field goal attempts, and 48.6 percent from the free-throw line.[http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2018/player/Alperen-Sengun Alperen SENGUN CENTER 2018 FIBA U16 EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIP.] He was also a part of the Turkish junior under-17 national team that competed at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], which was held in [[Argentina]]. Turkey finished that tournament in fifth place. In seven games played at that tournament, he averaged 15.9 points, 12.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.7 steals, and 0.9 blocks per game, in 28.6 minutes per game. He shot 58.3 percent from the field overall, 64.1 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 12.5 percent on 3-point field goal attempts, and 56.5 percent from the free-throw line.[http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/player/Alperen-Sengun Alperen SENGUN POWER FORWARD 2018 FIBA U17 BASKETBALL WORLD CUP.] Şengün also played at the [[2019 FIBA Under-18 European Championship]], with the [[Turkey men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Turkish junior under-18 national team]], which won the tournament's silver medal. He was also selected to that [[2019 FIBA Under-18 European Championship#Awards|competition's All-Tournament Team]], being the only Turkish player that was chosen for that honor. In seven games played at that tournament, he averaged 11.9 points, 9.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.6 steals, and 1.7 blocks per game, in 23.0 minutes per game. He shot 54.5 percent from the field overall, 59.2 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 16.7 percent on 3-point field goal attempts, and 59.5 percent from the free-throw line.[http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2019/player/Alperen-Sengun Alperen SENGUN POWER FORWARD 2019 FIBA U18 EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIP.] ===Turkish senior team=== In November 2020, Şengün joined the senior [[Turkish national basketball team|Turkish national team]], as he played with Turkey at the [[2022 EuroBasket Qualifiers]]. In four games played at the qualifiers, he averaged 12.0 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks, in 23.1 minutes per game. He shot 53.3 percent from the field overall, 51.9 percent on 2-point field goal attempts, 66.7 percent on 3-point field goal attempts, and 50.0 percent from the free-throw line.[http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/qualifiers/player/Alperen-Sengun Alperen SENGUN Besiktas ICRYPEX (TUR) STATS ALL STATS STATISTICS.] ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Youth club competitions=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:95%; text-align:right;" !
